From: Julia Kane <julia.kane@findata.com>

Cc: Markus Healy <m.healy@legalpartners.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed additions to incident / evidence transfer clause

Tessa — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Attaching a short redline and two specific asks from our legal team that we need to resolve before procurement can proceed: (1) confirmation we can receive a full forensic image of affected customer data for regulated EU accounts (we understand Redwood has subprocessors and cross-border controls), and (2) a described mechanism to securely transfer that evidence to our legal counsel or an appointed e-discovery vendor for regulator-facing investigations.

Our proposed language would require: initial notification within 48 hours, secure transfer capability within 5 business days after written request, and a supervisory review step if the material crosses EEA borders. We flagged that the DPA currently only contemplates log-level artifacts, not full images.

Attached: DPA_redline_v3.docx, evidence-transfer-checklist.pdf

Thanks — Julia
Julia Kane | Senior Counsel, FinData Solutions
julia.kane@findata.com | +44 20 5555 1234
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 12:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed additions to incident / evidence transfer clause

Julia — appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Quick summary of where Redwood sits and a pragmatic path forward:

- Incident notification: we can commit to initial customer-facing notification within 48–72 hours for confirmed incidents that materially affect customer data. For legal/regulatory notices we typically use a 72-hour window to ensure forensics are validated before statements go out.

- Forensic images vs logs: we do preserve full forensic images internally for severe incidents, but we have strict subprocessors and data residency constraints. We cannot automatically export full disk images for EEA-hosted customer data without a narrow, contracted process.

- Proposed mechanism (we think is acceptable to both sides):
  * Provide initial evidence package (logs, KV cache snapshot, hashed artifacts) within 5 business days of a written request.
  * If FinData requests full forensic images or disk-level artifacts, we will: (a) initiate an internal legal review and redaction pass, (b) coordinate transfer via a vetted e-discovery partner (we suggest EvidencePlus), and (c) provide the transfer under an access-limited escrow where EvidencePlus acts as custodian and only releases to your counsel upon jointly-signed transfer terms.

- Cross-border safeguards: for EEA data we require an SCC-reviewed transfer and customer authorization; transfers to non-EEA counsel will need either customer consent or an emergency legal order. For regulator-facing matters, Redwood will cooperate and provide evidence consistent with lawful requests and will notify customers unless prohibited.

I attached a suggested evidence-transfer checklist (see evidence-transfer-checklist.pdf) and a short draft clause (summary below) that narrows the triggers for full-image transfer and introduces the escrow/custodian flow to protect customer residency concerns.

Two asks back to you: confirm whether EvidencePlus is acceptable as the custodian, and confirm whether your procurement/legal team can accept a 72-hour initial notice (Redwood preference) rather than 48 hours for regulator notices so we can validate integrity.

If you’re OK, I’ll loop in Vivek for technical controls and Stephanie for escalation/SLA signoff.

— Tessa

Tessa — sending our annotated redline. Key comment: FinData cannot accept a grant of unilateral discretion to Redwood on cross-border transfer of evidentiary material. They need a contractual assurance that full-image transfers will be governed by (i) explicit customer consent or (ii) an escrow release to their counsel upon narrowly-scoped judicial/regulatory demand, and (iii) a forensic integrity attestation signed by Redwood’s forensics lead.

I also propose adding an independent third-party attestation clause in the event of cross-border handover — at minimum an accountable custodian (EvidencePlus) and a 10-business-day window for Redwood to produce hashed manifests and chain-of-custody records.

Marked-up: DPA_redline_v3.docx

We will also require a narrow scope for customer approval on EEA-hosted data and a standard redaction pass to remove non-relevant PII before transfer. EvidencePlus is already SOC-2 audited; I’ll add Vivek to confirm encryption-in-motion/in-rest controls.
